title: Piano Roll Tricks
intro: The Piano Roll is where MIDI becomes music. Most people use about ten percent of it. Here is the rest.

tips.t: Select all notes of the same pitch in one click
tips.d: Click a key on the keyboard graphic at the left of the Piano Roll and every note at that pitch in the region is selected. Perfect for grabbing all the hi‑hats at once.

tips.t: Select similar notes with Edit > Select > Same Note Pitch
tips.d: Select one note, then choose Edit > Select > Similar Events (⇧S) to grab the other notes of the same pitch — the selected note acts as the reference. Clicking the key on the Piano Roll keyboard does the same job in one gesture.

tips.t: Use Select > Inside Locators to grab a bar range
tips.d: Set the left and right locators around the bars you want, then choose Edit > Select > Inside Locators to select everything that falls between them. Precise, repeatable, no mouse accuracy required.

tips.t: Change note length numerically in the inspector
tips.d: Open the Event Float window — Window > Show Event Float, or ⌥E — to read and type a selected note's values numerically: Position, Status, Channel, Number (pitch), Velocity and Length. It floats above the Piano Roll, so you can nudge a value without leaving the editor.

tips.t: Type one length and every selected note follows
tips.d: Force Legato is a different job from setting one length: it stretches each note to end where the next one begins, which is not the same as giving every note an equal length. Reach for Edit > Trim > Note End to Following Notes (Force Legato) when you want notes to join up — not when you want them all the same size.

tips.t: Force legato to fix gappy pads
tips.d: Select the notes, then choose Edit > Trim > Note End to Following Notes (Force Legato) in the Piano Roll. Every note extends to end where the next one begins, and pads and basslines stop sounding stuttery instantly.

Select the notes and choose Edit > Trim > Note End to Remove Overlaps to Following Notes (8 Ticks Gap) in the Piano Roll. Logic shortens the note ends so nothing overlaps, leaving an eight-tick gap — which is what stops the phasing and stuck voices you get on hardware. There are matching versions for selected notes and for repeated notes.

Hold ⌥ while dragging any note or selection to copy rather than move — you can even ⌥-drag notes between two Piano Roll windows, or between two different projects. To stop a drag changing pitch, turn on Logic Pro > Settings > General > Editing > "Limit Dragging to One Direction In Piano Roll and Score": the direction you start in is then the only one you can move in. Pressing ⇧ while dragging switches that behaviour on and off; it is not a pitch lock on its own.

tips.t: Place a note between grid divisions
tips.d: Set Snap to a finer value — Ticks snaps to 1/3840 of a beat — or just press Control-Shift as you drag, which moves the note in tick steps and overrides the Snap value entirely. Do not reach for ⌃⌥-drag here: that is the Zoom tool, so it will move your view instead of your note.

tips.t: Change velocity by dragging with the Velocity tool
tips.d: Pick the Velocity tool from the Tool menu — or press and hold Control-Command to turn the Pointer into it temporarily — and drag up or down on a note. A help tag shows the velocity as you drag, and the line inside the note grows or shrinks. Turn on View > Set Note Color > By Velocity first if you want the note colour to track it too. Either way you never leave the Piano Roll.

tips.t: Draw a velocity ramp across a selection
tips.d: For a crescendo across a run of notes, select them all and drag one note upward with the Velocity tool. Logic moves the whole selection and keeps the relative differences between their velocity values, so you scale the shape of the performance instead of flattening it into a straight line.

tips.t: Show the automation lane inside the Piano Roll
tips.d: Click the Show/Hide Automation button in the Piano Roll Editor menu bar to open the Automation/MIDI lane under the notes. Choose modwheel, expression or sustain from the Automation/MIDI Parameter pop-up menu and edit that data right next to the notes it affects.

tips.t: Colour notes by velocity to read dynamics instantly
tips.d: In the Piano Roll's View menu, set note colour to Velocity. Flat parts become visibly, obviously flat.

tips.t: Quantise from the region inspector, not destructively
tips.d: The Quantize field in the Region inspector is non‑destructive and can be dialled back or removed at any point. Use it before you ever use the destructive version.

tips.t: Use Q‑Strength to keep the human feel
tips.d: Under the region's more‑options triangle, Q‑Strength at 60 to 80 percent pulls notes toward the grid without gluing them to it.

tips.t: Quantise only the notes that need it
tips.d: Select the offending notes in the Piano Roll and quantise the selection rather than the whole region. The good parts of the take stay untouched.
